tagline: Providing private mortgage insurance to help qualified borrowers achieve homeownership while mitigating credit risk for lenders
hero_kpi_rationale: Risk-In-Force (RIF) is the primary indicator of the actual size of the insured portfolio and the underlying risk covered, making it the fundamental driver of NMIH's value and growth trajectory in the mortgage insurance sector.

kpis.name: Risk-In-Force (RIF)
kpis.explanation: Total amount of risk the company covers on insured loans.
kpis.description: RIF reflects the company's potential liability in case of default. It is influenced by the volume of new insured loans and their LTV profiles.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth in the insured portfolio size

kpis.name: Insurance-In-Force (IIF)
kpis.explanation: Total amount of residential loans currently insured by the company.
kpis.description: IIF represents the future insurance premium revenue base. It grows with new insured loans and declines with repayments.

kpis.name: New Insurance Written (NIW)
kpis.explanation: Total value of new loans insured over a year.
kpis.description: NIW measures annual underwriting activity. It depends on the housing market and the company's market share.
kpis.signal: Significant annual flow of new insured loans

kpis.name: Number of Lender Customers
kpis.explanation: Total number of banks and lenders with which the company has an active contract.
kpis.description: A large and diversified customer base strengthens business resilience and growth capacity.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time and part-time employees.
kpis.description: A moderate workforce supports a highly specialized private mortgage insurance operation.
kpis.signal: Lean and efficient structure for a mortgage insurance operation

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €3.84 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €0.42 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Cash & Equivalents
kpis.description: Cash & equivalents extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Cash & equivalents of €0.04 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: New Lenders Activated
kpis.explanation: Number of new lenders that began using the company's insurance during the year.
kpis.description: Activations reflect the company's ability to convert agreements into actual business activity. A decline of 23.7% compared to 118 in 2024 may indicate market slowdown or increased competition.

kpis.name: Number of Lender Customers
kpis.explanation: Total number of banks and lenders with which the company has an active contract.
kpis.description: A large and diversified customer base strengthens business resilience and growth capacity. The portfolio includes national banks, regional banks, credit unions, and non-bank lenders.

risks.title: Intense competition in private mortgage insurance
risks.summary: Increased competition from other private or public insurers could reduce our market share, revenues, and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is listed as a top risk factor and described as critical to achieving business objectives. The language is repeated and reinforced, particularly regarding pricing pressure and underwriting policies. The 'Competition' category is highly weighted in the MI sector.

risks.title: Loss of GSE recognition
risks.summary: If the GSEs no longer recognize us as an approved insurer, our access to the primary market would be severely compromised.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned as an existential risk related to PMIERs and GSE approval. Loss of approval would have a direct impact on business operations. Strong language used ('adversely impact', 'could reduce revenues').

risks.title: Alternatives to private mortgage insurance
risks.summary: Lenders may choose public or structural alternatives that reduce or eliminate the need for private insurance.
risks.score_rationale: Described in detail with multiple examples (FHA, VA, self-insurance, loan structures). Structural risk to MI demand. Less intense than direct competition but still major.

risks.title: Failure of claim reserves
risks.summary: Incorrect estimation of claims may lead to unexpected losses and severely impact profitability.
risks.score_rationale: Strong language: 'actual claim payments may materially exceed reserves', 'unexpected charges to income'. Core risk for an insurer. Key position in the 10-K, with direct link to financial results.

risks.title: Dependence on technology partners
risks.summary: Inability to maintain competitive technology may harm customer relationships and growth.
risks.score_rationale: Key operational risk related to customer connectivity and proprietary platforms. Mention of customer loss if technology is insufficient. Less existential than credit or regulatory risks.

risks.title: Reinsurance counterparty risks
risks.summary: A reinsurer default or loss of capital credit could weaken our financial and regulatory position.
risks.score_rationale: Impact on solvency through loss of capital credit. Mention of counterparty exposure and downgrades. Risk amplified by dependence on GSE and Wisconsin OCI decisions.

risks.title: Cyber threats and unauthorized disclosure
risks.summary: A security breach could result in data loss, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.
risks.score_rationale: Mention of operational risk involving confidential data. Moderate language but implicit consequences on regulation and reputation. Less central than direct financial risks.

ai_positioning.summary: NMIH does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
